task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific variant-bucket value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing, material collection, tuple preparation and runtime salt-config materialization, whose own body constructs the target observable variant name rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the console or localStorage.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target variant is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output and storage persistence.
The assign route selects its live salt-bearing configuration only after click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state are captured.
The storage key is assembled from character-code arrays, obscuring the persistence destination.

The click path crosses delegated event handling, action routing, gate checks, user/flag material collection with page-context snapshot, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, variant bucketing, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same assign interaction emits non-target flag.exposure/flag.audit objects carrying variant-like values before the target flag.assign object.
An exposure logger emits a variant-styled probe via console.debug, and an inactive shadow-roll chain remains reachable-looking without feeding the target variant field.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the variant constructor receives its salt.
The final sink receives an already assigned variant name after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: route-selected salt-mixed murmur-style bucket hash over user and flag material mapped to an 8-arm experiment variant
behavior_category.reason: The observable variant is a deterministic but one-way bucketing derivation: the user key, flag key and runtime-materialized salt are folded through a murmur-style 32-bit mix whose modulo-8 bucket selects the arm label. The variant cannot be decoded back into the hashing material, and the value never enters an outbound request; the localStorage record under ff_assignment only mirrors the console field.

near_categories.why_not: The variant is not an encoding of a normalized assignment state; it is a one-way bucketed derivation of the hashing material. Same input always maps to the same variant, but no receiver can decode or verify the variant back into the user/flag state.
The primary observable does not enter any outbound request; this case has no network egress at all and the only secondary sink is localStorage, which mirrors the console value.
The chain uses local DOM/form state and page context as routing input, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
The output is a short arm label, not a byte array; byte-payload-like code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target variant field.
